skill.name: golang-observability
skill.description: Golang everyday observability — the always-on signals in production. Covers structured logging with slog, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry distributed tracing, continuous profiling with pprof/Pyroscope, server-side RUM event tracking, alerting, and Grafana dashboards. Apply when instrumenting Go services for production monitoring, setting up metrics or alerting, adding OpenTelemetry tracing, correlating logs with traces, migrating legacy loggers (zap/logrus/zerolog) to slog, adding observability to new features, or implementing GDPR/CCPA-compliant tracking with Customer Data Platforms (CDP). Not for temporary deep-dive performance investigation (→ See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-benchmark` and `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-performance` skills).
skill.summary: Instrument Go services with structured logs, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, profiling, and privacy-aware analytics guidance.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives involving Markdown, Go syntax, PromQL expressions, and evaluation fixtures; one profiling URL example encourages credentials over plaintext HTTP. Five additional findings cover credential logging, missing authorization in privacy examples, incomplete erasure reporting, unbounded metric labels, and misleading identifier privacy claims. No evidence found of malicious execution, unauthorized exfiltration intent, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The profiling configuration illustrates credentials in a plaintext HTTP URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS with certificate validation and configure authentication separately from the collector URL.

remediation.issue: The profiling startup log emits PYROSCOPE_URL, which the example allows to contain credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Log only an allowlisted hostname and port; never log URL user information, tokens, or secret query parameters.

remediation.issue: Privacy handlers use a caller-selected user ID without showing authentication or ownership checks.
remediation.suggestion: Authenticate callers and enforce subject ownership or explicit administrative authorization before exporting or deleting data.

remediation.issue: Analytics deletion failures still produce a completion log and successful response.
remediation.suggestion: Persist deletion jobs, retry failed vendor operations, and report pending or failed erasure until all required systems confirm deletion.

remediation.issue: The latency middleware labels histograms with raw request paths despite later cardinality warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Use normalized route templates and bounded fallback labels in every middleware example, including unknown routes and methods.

remediation.issue: The RUM guide describes internal user identifiers as not personally identifiable information.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that linkable user identifiers remain personal data; apply access controls, minimization, retention, and deletion requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Profiling Startup Log Can Expose Collector Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The success log emits the entire PYROSCOPE_URL. The same example permits embedded credentials, exposing them to log storage and downstream collectors.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The log directly reads the same environment variable illustrated with URL credentials. Exposure occurs when users adopt that documented credential format.

semantic_findings.title: Privacy Handler Examples Omit Subject Authorization
semantic_findings.description: Export and deletion handlers use chi.URLParam(r, "id") without checking caller ownership. Without external authorization, callers could export or delete another user's data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both handlers pass caller-selected IDs directly to sensitive repository operations. No authorization middleware is shown, so deployment exploitability depends on integration.

semantic_findings.title: Erasure Handler Reports Success After Vendor Failures
semantic_findings.description: Vendor deletion errors are logged without retry or failure propagation. The handler still reports completion and HTTP 204, potentially retaining analytics data after apparent erasure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both vendor error branches continue to an unconditional completion log and success response. No durable retry or pending deletion state appears.

semantic_findings.title: Latency Middleware Creates Unbounded Metric Labels
semantic_findings.description: The latency middleware uses r.URL.Path directly as a histogram label. Attacker-controlled paths can create excessive time series and exhaust monitoring resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example records raw paths instead of route templates. Later cardinality warnings do not change this copyable middleware example.

semantic_findings.title: Analytics Guidance Misclassifies Linkable User Identifiers
semantic_findings.description: The guide calls internal user_id values "not PII" and repeats this in its privacy checklist. Linkable identifiers remain personal data despite replacing email.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples link identifiers to specific users and business events. Calling them non-personal can incorrectly exempt analytics data from privacy safeguards.

content.user_title: Instrument Go Services for Production Observability
content.value_statement: Missing telemetry makes production failures difficult to diagnose. This skill guides Go instrumentation with structured logs, metrics, traces, profiling, and analytics privacy considerations.
actual_capabilities: Guide structured slog logging, context-aware calls, and incremental migration from zap, logrus, or zerolog.
Explain Prometheus metric types, histogram buckets, naming conventions, bounded labels, and PromQL comments.
Guide OpenTelemetry provider setup, spans, context propagation, error recording, sampling, and metric exemplars.
Describe protected pprof endpoints and environment-controlled Pyroscope continuous profiling.
Provide alerting and Grafana guidance, including golden signals and multi-window error-budget burn rates.
Explain PostHog and Segment event tracking, consent checks, and data export and deletion workflows.
limitations: Provides instructions and examples, not a deployed monitoring platform or bundled executable collector.
Requires project-specific integration, compatible Go libraries, and separately configured telemetry backends.
Examples need security review, especially credential handling, metric cardinality, and privacy endpoint authorization.
Does not guarantee legal compliance or replace specialist performance investigations and privacy review.

use_cases.title: Instrument a New Go API
use_cases.description: Add request metrics, structured logs, and trace spans before releasing a new service.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Alerting
use_cases.description: Review metric labels, latency histograms, and error-budget alerts to reduce monitoring noise and identify coverage gaps.

use_cases.title: Review Analytics Data Flows
use_cases.description: Evaluate server-side event tracking, consent handling, identifiers, and deletion workflows with engineering and privacy stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go handler for structured slog fields, context propagation, log levels, and sensitive data. Explain the smallest useful changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Request Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Instrument this Go router with request counters and latency histograms. Use route templates, bounded labels, suitable buckets, and PromQL comments.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Logs and Traces
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go service's OpenTelemetry setup. Preserve context across database and HTTP calls, correlate slog records, and propose sampling and exemplar settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: correlate telemetry across service boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Go repository across logs, metrics, traces, profiles, and analytics. Report evidence, security gaps, and prioritized fixes without changing production settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: assess observability across a repository.

output_examples.input: Review request metrics that label every request with its full path and user ID.
output: Both labels can create unbounded time series and increase monitoring memory use.
Replace raw paths with route templates and remove user IDs from metric labels.
Use access-controlled traces for necessary user-level correlation.

output_examples.input: Our 99.9% availability alert produces noise during short error spikes.
output: Review the availability definition and error-budget calculation.
Pair short and long burn-rate windows to distinguish sustained degradation from brief spikes.
Validate thresholds and persistence durations against historical traffic before enabling paging.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed production profiling integration.
output: Keep pprof on a protected internal listener.
Use encrypted collector transport and redact credentials from startup logs.
Start with selected profile types and measure overhead on a limited replica set.

best_practices: Validate library APIs and telemetry examples against the versions installed in your project.
Use bounded metric labels, intentional sampling, and tested alert thresholds before production rollout.
Protect profiling endpoints, redact secrets, and verify authorization and consent before processing user telemetry.
anti_patterns: Copying examples into production without security review or integration tests.
Using raw paths, user IDs, or request IDs as metric labels.
Treating pseudonymous identifiers as anonymous data or assuming analytics examples guarantee compliance.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares compatibility with Codex and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install monitoring infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples; you configure collectors, storage, dashboards, credentials, and deployment separately.

faq.question: Which telemetry signals does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers structured logs, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, profiling, and server-side analytics.

faq.question: Can it help migrate existing Go loggers?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes incremental migration from zap, logrus, and zerolog to slog through bridge handlers and call-site changes.

faq.question: Does its analytics guidance guarantee GDPR or CCPA compliance?
faq.answer: No. Obtain privacy review, treat linkable user identifiers as personal data, and validate consent, authorization, retention, and deletion behavior.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for production without changes?
faq.answer: No. Review credentials, transport encryption, endpoint authorization, metric labels, and failure handling before adapting them.
